[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [source_identity] ""May the blessing of the one who is perishing come upon me" (Job 29:13)" vs "Εὐλογία κτλ.": Greek has only "Blessing etc." with no verse specified; translator supplies Job 29:13 without manuscript basis.; [completeness] "missing section break and numerals" vs "ιεʹ ... ι ʹ": Greek section numbers 15 and 10 are omitted; these are source text elements.; [agency] ""I was eyes to the blind, and feet to the lame" (Job 29:15)" vs "Ὀφθαλμὸς ἤμην τυφλῶν, ποὺς δὲ χωλῶν": Greek has singular "eye" (ὀφθαλμὸς), not "eyes"; translator changes number.; [agency] "he opened blind minds, and he helped those maimed in soul" vs "τυφλὰς διανοίας διήνοιγε, καὶ ὠφείλει τοὺς πεπηρωμένους": Greek has first singular implied (Job speaking), not "he"; translator shifts to third person.; [agency] "he himself became their eye" vs "αὐτὸς αὐτῶν ἐγίνετο ὀφθαλμός": Greek has first singular (Job), not "he"; translator shifts to third person.; [agency] "He gave feet... he became their foot, and he led both by the hand" vs "ἐχαρίζετο... ἐγίνετο... ἐχειραγώγει": Greek has first singular throughout (Job speaking), not "he"; translator shifts to third person. | part 2/5: [agency] "I stood before another's battle" vs "ἀλλοτρίας προϊστάμην μάχης": Subject is ambiguous; could be 'he stood before' not 'I'; [scripture] "Psalm 57:7 [58:6]" vs "τὰς μύλας τῶν λεόντων": LXX Psalm 57:5 or 57:6, not 57:7; Hebrew 58:6 is correct; [completeness] "now they admonish me in turn, whose fathers I despised" vs "Νυνὶ δὲ κατεγέλασάν μου ἐλάχιστοι": Invented clause: 'they admonish me in turn, whose fathers I despised' not in source; [negation] "not only with money, not only with food" vs "οὐ μέχρι χρημάτων, οὐδὲ μέχρι τροφῆς": 'not only' misrenders οὐ/οὐδὲ as concessive rather than absolute negation | part 3/5: [source_identity] ""But now the least of men have laughed at me"" vs "νῦν νουθετοῦσί με ἐν μέρει": English adds 'least of men have laughed at me' not in source; source has 'now they admonish me in part/turn'; [negation] ""He did not use contempt"" vs "Οὐ χρώμενος τῇ ἐξουδενώσει": Participial syntax: 'not using contempt' not 'he did not use contempt'; changes grammatical construction; [agency] ""he knew them clearly"" vs "ἀλλὰ σαφῶς εἰδὼς αὐτούς": Subject is Job continuing from participle, not new 'he'; but contextually clear; [scripture] ""Every evildoer is despised before him"" vs "Ἐξουδενοῦται ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πᾶς πονηρευόμενος": No scripture reference given in English for this quotation; [completeness] ""2, 3" omitted entirely" vs "βʹ, γʹ": Verse numbers dropped without indication; [modality] ""what is it to me?"" vs "ἱνατί μοι;": 'ἱνατί' = 'for what purpose/why' not 'what is it'; interrogative of purpose not identity; [mistranslation] ""Their end has perished upon them"" vs "ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἀπώλετο συντέλεια": 'συντέλεια' = completion/consummation/fulfillment, not 'end'; 'their end' misrepresents; [mistranslation] ""into a waterless place"" vs "ἄνυδρον": 'ἄνυδρον' modifies 'συνοχήν' (waterless distress), not separate 'place'; wrong syntactic attachment; [negation] ""But I did not ask for any help from them"" vs "Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ᾔτησά τινα ἐπικουρίαν... παρ' αὐτῶν": 'οὐδέ' = 'not even', stronger than 'not'; 'not even did I ask' is correct force; [modality] ""so that for this reason they would use such words against me"" vs "ἵνα διὰ τοῦτο τοιούτοις πρὸς ἐμὲ χρήσωνται ῥήμασιν": 'χρήσωνται' = future indicative, not optative/would; 'they will use' not 'would use'; [agency] ""They long ago owed a penalty, being wicked"" vs "οἵ γε πάλαι δίκην ἐχρεώστουν, πονηροὶ ὄντες": Subject is still Job's mockers (οἵ γε = 'who indeed'), not new 'they'; but contextually recoverable; [mistranslation] ""the punishment flew away from them"" vs "ἀπέπτη ἀπ' αὐτῶν ἡ τιμωρία": 'ἀπέπτη' = flew away/escaped; correct but 'punishment flew away' is odd; means penalty escaped them; [mistranslation] ""to become parents of the good"" vs "γεννηταὶ γενέσθαι τοῦ καλοῦ": 'γεννηταί' = parents/begetters, but 'γενέσθαι' = to become; 'to become parents' correct but 'of the good' = 'of the beautiful/fine/noble'; [mistranslation] ""those who yesterday, or a little before, had fled from the desert and from disasters"" vs "οἱ ἐχθές που καὶ πρὸ ὀλίγου, τῆς ἐρήμου καὶ τῶν συμφορῶν ἐκπεφευγότες": 'ἐχθές που' = 'yesterday somewhere' not 'yesterday, or a little before'; 'πρὸ ὀλίγου' = 'before little' = 'a little before' but 'που' = 'somewhere' dropped | part 4/5: [completeness] "“For if only I could lay hands on myself” (Job 30:24)" vs "κδʹ": Greek ends at κδʹ (24), a section number; this clause belongs to next section, not in source passage; [scripture] "(Job 30:2)" vs "Ἐπ' αὐτοὺς ἀπώλετο συντέλεια": Verse reference missing; should be Job 30:2 or 30:3 LXX; [completeness] "379" vs "379 δʹ": Page number 379 dropped from translation | part 5/5: [source_identity] ""For if only I could lay hands on myself" (Job 30:24)" vs "Εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον δυναίμην ἐμαυτὸν χειρώσασθαι": Job 30:24 is wrong; this is Job 30:24 in Hebrew but LXX numbering differs; actually LXX Job 30:24 begins differently. The citation should be checked against LXX.; [completeness] "he is not even ashamed before a crowd of people" vs "οὐδὲ πλῆθος συνόδου αἰσχυνόμενος": Dropped 'standing' (Ἕστηκα); the participles show simultaneous standing and crying, not just shamelessness.; [agency] "I have forgotten my own nature" vs "ἠγνόησα τὴν φύσιν τὴν οἰκείαν": 'ἠγνόησα' means 'I was ignorant of/I failed to recognize,' not 'I have forgotten' (active neglect vs. passive ignorance).; [scripture] "(Job 31:6–7)" vs "Κεφ. ΛΑʹ, ʹ, ζʹ": The Greek has 'Ch. 31, 1, 7' — verse 1 and 7, not 6–7; the citation '6–7' does not match the source's '1, 7'.; [modality] "No one could say that because I used my wealth" vs "οὐκ ἔχοι τις εἰπεῖν, ὅτι τῷ πλούτῳ... ἀποχρησάμενος": 'οὐκ ἔχοι' is optative of possibility ('no one would be able to say'), not past 'could'; and the participles are causal grounds Job rejects, not admission.

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'May the blessing of the one who is perishing come upon me (Job 29:13)' expands the catena's abbreviation Εὐλογία κτλ. with the verse it abbreviates (LXX Job 29:13). 'He opened blind minds … he himself became their eye … he led both by the hand' renders the third-person imperfects διήνοιγε, ὠφέλει, ἐγίνετο, ἐχαρίζετο, ἐχειραγώγει, in which the commentator describes Job. 'Psalm 57:7 [58:6]' is correct for τὰς μύλας τῶν λεόντων. Job 30:1 ('But now the least of men have laughed at me; now they admonish me in turn, whose fathers I despised') and 30:24 (Εἰ γὰρ ὄφελον δυναίμην ἐμαυτὸν χειρώσασθαι) are LXX lemmata quoted in the Greek. 'Job 31:6–7' follows the lemma Κεφ. ΛΑʹ, [ϛ]ʹ, ζʹ, where the stigma has dropped out in print. The rest (singular ὀφθαλμός, συντέλεια as 'end', ἐχθές που) is idiom.
